items.title: docs: fix the PageSpeed findings on the landing page
items.body:
## What was wrong

PageSpeed Insights on https://faststream.ag2.ai/ (mobile): performance 70, accessibility 87, best practices 96, SEO 92, agentic browsing 1/2. Desktop scores 97 on performance, and Chrome's field data passes Core Web Vitals (LCP 0.8 s, INP 28 ms, CLS 0), so what fails is the mobile lab run and a set of page-level audits. A local Lighthouse run named the elements:

| Audit | Cause |
|---|---|
| console error on every page | Material's outdated-banner script runs `new URL("{{ base_url }}")`, and mkdocs renders `base_url` relative (`.`, `../..`): `TypeError: Invalid URL` |
| dialog without a name (also the only agentic-browsing failure) | Material's search `div.md-search role="dialog"` has no `aria-label` |
| link text | two landing page links read "here" |
| contrast < 4.5 | slate code highlight: keyword `#6791e0` 4.09, function `#c973d9` 4.23, constant `#9383e2` 4.01–4.48 on the code and highlighted-line backgrounds; the footer copyright 3.66 |
| links told apart by colour alone | links in running text, 1.51:1 against the surrounding text |
| CLS 0.14 | the landing badges have no size and push the page down as they load |
| LCP 6–8 s | the LCP element is the trendshift.io badge; the Google Fonts stylesheet blocks the first paint |
| touch targets | every code line number is a 16×18 px link (`anchor_linenums`), 104 on the landing page |

## What this does

- `overrides/partials/javascripts/outdated.html`: `new URL(base_url, location)`
- `overrides/partials/search.html`: Material 9.7.7's partial plus `aria-label="Search"` on the dialog. The header asks for a re-sync on theme upgrades.
- the two "here" links name their target (`CLI features`, `FastAPI plugin guide`)
- the `privacy` plugin self-hosts Google Fonts only (`assets_include: fonts.googleapis.com/*, fonts.gstatic.com/*`, `links: false`), so there are no requests to Google and no third-party stylesheet in the critical path. The other external images stay live.
- landing badges carry `width`/`height` taken from the current SVGs; trendshift gets `fetchpriority="high"`
- slate: `--md-code-hl-{keyword,function,constant}-color` lightened to the smallest value that clears 4.5:1 on both code backgrounds, and `--md-footer-fg-color--lighter` goes to 0.56 alpha. The light scheme already passes and is unchanged.
- links inside `p`, `li` and `td` are underlined; buttons and image links (badges) are not
- `anchor_linenums` is off: line numbers become plain text. The docs had one link to a code line, the FastAPI page's "line 20", and #3154 turns that into plain text, since it pointed at the wrong block anyway.

## Checks

Lighthouse (mobile) on local builds of `main` and of this branch, two runs each:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Accessibility | 87 | **97** |
| SEO | 92 | **100** |
| Agentic browsing | 67 | **100** |
| CLS | 0.01–0.02 | **0** |
| Performance | 54–60 | 62–63 |

- Best practices stays at 96 locally only because the local server has no mike `versions.json` (a 404 in the console); the `TypeError` is gone. The 104 line-number targets were measured before `anchor_linenums` came off, so accessibility should move again.
- Absolute performance numbers are lower than PSI's because `http.server` doesn't compress; the before/after delta is what counts. Most of what still blocks rendering is Material's own `main.css`.
- On the built site: fonts come from `assets/external/`, the outdated script has `location`, the search dialog has `aria-label=Search`, and code line numbers are `<span>`s.
- Not fixable on GitHub Pages: a 10-minute cache on every asset, and the 73 KiB of unused JS that is Google Analytics itself.

items.title: Material reference parity: syntax and markup contracts for annotations, grids, buttons, diagrams, icons, and lightbox
items.body:
## Context

Bartleby's next goal is to render every feature on the mkdocs-material reference (https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/reference/) in both of its bundled themes. The decision for the split (Mason, 2026-10-14): markwright is the batteries-included Markdown library and owns the authoring syntax and the HTML contract for each feature; Bartleby owns CSS, JavaScript, and bundled assets. That is the same shape as the click-to-load embeds contract in 0.3.0. markwright's invariant that it ships no JavaScript and no CSS stays as written.

This issue records the research so the markwright side can be specified and planned here. Bartleby's spec (Goal 10) references this issue and will consume whatever release carries the work.

## How mkdocs-material Builds Each Feature

None of the reference features is a Markdown-library feature in mkdocs-material. Each is stock pymdownx or `attr_list` output plus the theme's own CSS and TypeScript (paths under `src/templates/assets/` in the mkdocs-material repo).

| Feature | Author syntax | Markup source | What the theme adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annotations | `{ .annotate }` on a block with `(1)` markers, or `# (1)!` in a code comment, then an ordered list after the block | `attr_list`, `md_in_html`, `superfences` | `javascripts/components/content/annotation`: swaps markers for `<aside class="md-annotation">` and positions a tooltip; CSS in `stylesheets/main/components/_tooltip.scss` |
| Buttons | `[Text](url){ .md-button .md-button--primary }` | `attr_list` | CSS only (`components/_form.scss`) |
| Grids and cards | `<div class="grid cards" markdown>` around a list, or `<div class="grid" markdown>` with `{ .card }` children | `attr_list`, `md_in_html` | CSS only (`modifiers/_grid.scss`): `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr))`, `display: contents` on the list |
| Diagrams | A `mermaid` fence | `superfences` custom fence with `fence_code_format`, yielding `<pre class="mermaid"><code>` | `components/content/mermaid`: fetches `mermaid@11` from unpkg on demand and replaces the `<pre>` with an SVG in a closed shadow root |
| Icons | `:material-x:`, `:octicons-x-16:`, `:fontawesome-brands-x:`, `:simple-x:` with optional `{ .lg .middle }` | `pymdownx.emoji` with `material.extensions.emoji.twemoji` (index built by walking `.icons/**/*.svg`, path with `/` replaced by `-`) and `to_svg` (inlines the file as `<span class="twemoji"><svg>`) | CSS only (`extensions/pymdownx/_emoji.scss`) |
| Images | `{ align=left width=300 }`, `{ loading=lazy }`, `<figure markdown="span">`, `/// caption`, `#only-light` | `attr_list`, `md_in_html`, `pymdownx.blocks.caption` | CSS for alignment and figures; the lightbox is the separate `mkdocs-glightbox` plugin |
| Math | `$...$`, `$$...$$` | `pymdownx.arithmatex` with `generic: true` | CSS only; the author adds MathJax or KaTeX from unpkg themselves |
| Tooltips | `[link](url "Title")`, `*[HTML]: ...`, `:icon:{ title="..." }`, footnotes | `abbr`, `attr_list`, `footnotes`, `snippets` | `components/tooltip2`: moves `title` into `div.md-tooltip2`; footnote tooltips clone the `li#fn:x` body |
| Code blocks | `title=`, `linenums=`, `hl_lines=`, `.copy`, `.select` | `pymdownx.highlight` (`anchor_linenums`, `line_spans`) | `components/content/code`: copy button (ClipboardJS), line selection with a URL hash |
| Content tabs | `=== "Label"` | `pymdownx.tabbed` with `alternate_style` | `components/content/tabs`: indicator, scroll, and `content.tabs.link` (same-label tabs switch together, stored per site) |
| Data tables | Pipe tables | `tables` | A scroll wrapper; sorting is the author-added `tablesort` from unpkg |

Pure CSS in mkdocs-material: buttons, grids, icons, image alignment and captions, abbreviation underline. Needs JavaScript: annotations, code copy and select, tabs indicator and linking, tooltips, table wrapper, mermaid. Fetched from a CDN by mkdocs-material or by the author: mermaid, MathJax or KaTeX, tablesort.

## What Would Live in markwright

These are the pieces where a syntax or a markup contract is missing, so a host theme has nothing stable to style. Listed as candidates, not decisions.

1. Annotations: a source-stage or HTML-stage extension that turns `(1)` markers plus the following ordered list into inline markup with stable hooks (for example an `<aside>` per marker carrying the list item's content, with a class and a data attribute), so a host needs only CSS and a small positioning script. The code-comment form (`# (1)!`) needs the comment stripped the way mkdocs-material does. The HTML `popover` attribute plus CSS anchor positioning may make a host script unnecessary; worth a look.
2. Grids and cards: a block syntax (`pymdownx.blocks` is already inside `pymdown-extensions`, so no new dependency) that emits a container with stable classes, in place of the raw `<div markdown>` wrapper.
3. Buttons: a documented class contract on a link, or a small directive; the markup is a plain `<a>` with classes either way.
4. Diagrams: a `mermaid` fence in the fence extension, emitting `<pre>` with a stable class and the source intact, so the host can hand it to mermaid.js.
5. Icons: an emoji index and generator in the style of `material.extensions.emoji`, built from icon directories the host passes as an option (Bartleby's themes ship Octicons and Lucide and know their directories), emitting an inline SVG with a stable wrapper class and `aria-hidden`.
6. Lightbox: an opt-in per image (an attribute or a directive) that wraps the image in a link with a stable hook; the host supplies a `<dialog>`.

Nothing to add in markwright for math (`arithmatex` already writes the delimiters; the typesetter is JavaScript), tooltips and footnote tooltips (the `title` and footnote markup exist), code select, linked tabs, or sortable tables (all host scripts).

## What Bartleby Will Do

Bundle KaTeX (about 300 KB with fonts), mermaid (about 2.8 MB, loaded only on pages with a diagram), and tablesort (5 KB), all MIT and credited; ship the CSS and scripts for every contract above in both bundled themes; show each feature on the scaffold's tour page with a visible result; and keep its accessibility audit and lint at zero. Icon packs stay Octicons and Lucide (decided 2026-10-14).

## Things the markwright Spec May Need to Say

- The roadmap says work is issue-driven; this would be a goal with its own plan.
- The dependency list stays frozen; everything above fits inside `markdown` and `pymdown-extensions`.
- The do-markdownit parity invariant covers the existing eight extensions; these are additive.
- A class prefix convention (`mw-`) for the new contracts, since the existing embed classes are listed under Deferred for the same rename.
- Each new extension documented on the docs site with its demo, as the existing eight are, so Bartleby's tour can mirror it.

## Open Questions

- Annotation markup: inline the list items at the marker, or leave the list in place and link by id?
- Icons: does the extension take directories, or a mapping of prefix to directory, so `:octicons-x-16:` and `:lucide-x:` resolve against different packs?
- Lightbox: attribute on the image (`{ lightbox }`) or a wrapping directive?
- Whether a `/// cards` block or the mkdocs-material `<div class="grid cards" markdown>` form is the one markwright documents (both could render).

items.title: change: unique source code span and codeline IDs
items.body: ### Is your change request related to a problem? Please describe. When using `show_source` the code snippet has a `span` and `codelineno` ID per line, e.g. ``. If referencing the same line in two different code snippets (e.g. the same line from two different modules given on the same page or the same method being referenced as it is inherited from the parent abstract base class in a module), there are duplicate instances of the same spand and codeline ID. Accessibility checkers complain about this, and with good reason! ### Describe the solution you'd like Ideally, each source code snippet would have some kind of unique code (maybe a random hash?) that is added to the IDs. ### Describe alternatives you've considered For now, I've simply ignored these types of IDs in my Accessibility checker, but it is non-ideal... ### Additional context

items.title: docs: Zensical Documentation Site with Scientific Visualization Suite
items.body:
# Zensical Documentation Site with Scientific Visualization Suite

## Summary

Create a modern documentation site using **Zensical** (the next-gen SSG from the Material for MkDocs team), leveraging its **modern design system** with Material Design 3 color palette compatibility, featuring state-of-the-art scientific visualization for optimizer benchmark results inspired by COCO/IOHprofiler standards.

> **Why Zensical?** The squidfunk team (creators of Material for MkDocs) launched Zensical in November 2025 as their next-generation static site generator. It addresses MkDocs' architectural limitations and supply chain risks (unmaintained since Aug 2024) while providing 5x faster rebuilds, blazing-fast Disco search, and full `mkdocs.yml` compatibility.

---

## Technology Stack

### Core Framework
| Component | Technology | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| **SSG** | Zensical | Next-gen from squidfunk team, Rust+Python, 5x faster rebuilds |
| **Build Engine** | ZRX | Differential build engine - backbone of Zensical (Open Source) |
| **Theme** | Modern Design | Built-in brandable design, breaks from Material Design aesthetic |
| **Colors** | Material Design 3 | Built-in `deep purple` + `teal` palette with dark/light toggle |
| **Search** | Disco | Blazing-fast client-side search with filtering & aggregation |
| **Math** | MathJax/KaTeX | Full LaTeX support for optimization equations |
| **Diagrams** | Mermaid | Native support inherited from Material for MkDocs |
| **API Docs** | mkdocstrings | Tim (@pawamoy) joining Zensical team for API reference |

### Built-in Color Palette (Zero Custom CSS)

Zensical inherits Material for MkDocs' battle-tested color system:

```yaml
# zensical.yml (compatible with mkdocs.yml)
theme:
  palette:
    # Light mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      scheme: default
      primary: deep purple
      accent: teal
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-7
        name: Switch to dark mode
    # Dark mode  
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      scheme: slate
      primary: deep purple
      accent: teal
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-4
        name: Switch to light mode
```

**Deep Purple + Teal Palette:**
- `deep purple` (#673AB7) - Primary: headers, links, navigation accents
- `teal` (#009688) - Accent: buttons, highlights, interactive elements
- `slate` - Dark mode background scheme
- Automatic WCAG AA contrast compliance

### Zensical-Specific Advantages
| Feature | Benefit for useful-optimizer |
|---------|------------------------------|
| **ZRX Differential Builds** | Only rebuild changed pages - critical for 100+ algorithm docs |
| **Disco Search** | Filtering by category, aggregation, fuzzy matching for 100+ algorithms |
| **mkdocs.yml Compatibility** | Minimal migration effort from existing MkDocs projects |
| **Module System (Early 2026)** | Replace plugins with deterministic, parallelizable modules |
| **Component System (2026)** | Custom Vue-like components for scientific visualizations |
| **CommonMark Rust Parser** | Significant Markdown performance improvements |
| **mkdocstrings Integration** | Native Python docstring extraction (Google-style) |

---

## Scientific Visualization Architecture

### Overview

Three-tier visualization system matching academic benchmarking standards (COCO, IOHprofiler, Nevergrad):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TIER 1: Scientific Standard                   │
│  ┌─────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌───────┐ │
│  │  ECDF   │ │ Convergence  │ │ Violin │ │ Friedman │ │Wilcox │ │
│  │  Curve  │ │ w/Confidence │ │  Plot  │ │ Heatmap  │ │Matrix │ │
│  └─────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────┘ └──────────┘ └───────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    TIER 2: Interactive Exploration               │
│  ┌─────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌──────┐ │
│  │   3D    │ │   Search     │ │ Parallel │ │ Perf.   │ │Radar │ │
│  │Landscape│ │  Trajectory  │ │  Coords  │ │ Profile │ │Chart │ │
│  └─────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────┘ └─────────┘ └──────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    TIER 3: Dashboard Integration                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Unified Dashboard: Algorithm Selection → Multi-View Panel  │ │
│  │  Statistical Summary: Avg | Std | Best | Worst | Time | FE  │ │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Tier 1: Scientific Standard Visualizations

### 1.1 Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (ECDF)

The gold standard for optimizer comparison (COCO platform standard):

```typescript
interface ECDFConfig {
  targetPrecisions: number[];  // e.g., [1e-1, 1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-7]
  maxBudget: number;           // Max function evaluations
  logScale: boolean;           // Log-scale x-axis
  confidenceBands: boolean;    // Bootstrap confidence intervals
}
```

**Implementation:**
- X-axis: log₁₀(#f-evaluations / dimension)
- Y-axis: Proportion of (function, target) pairs solved
- Multiple line series per algorithm
- Shaded confidence bands (95% CI)

### 1.2 Convergence Curves with Confidence Bands

```typescript
interface ConvergenceConfig {
  runs: number;                 // Default: 30 independent runs
  showConfidenceBand: boolean;  // ±1 std or 95% CI
  showMedian: boolean;          // Median line + IQR shading
  logYAxis: boolean;            // Log-scale fitness
  aggregation: 'mean' | 'median' | 'best';
}
```

**Metrics per iteration:**
- Mean ± Standard Deviation
- Median with IQR (Q1-Q3) shading
- Best/Worst envelope

### 1.3 Boxplot / Violin Plot Comparison

Statistical distribution of final fitness values across 30 runs:

```typescript
interface BoxplotConfig {
  showViolin: boolean;       // Kernel density overlay
  showPoints: boolean;       // Scatter individual runs
  showOutliers: boolean;     // Mark statistical outliers
  sortBy: 'median' | 'mean' | 'name';
}
```

### 1.4 Friedman Test Heatmap

Rank-based statistical comparison across multiple functions:

```typescript
interface FriedmanHeatmapConfig {
  functions: string[];        // Benchmark functions
  algorithms: string[];       // Optimizers to compare
  cellContent: 'rank' | 'avg_rank' | 'p_value';
  colorScale: 'viridis' | 'material';  // Material Design colors
}
```

**Statistical Protocol:**
1. Run each algorithm 30 times per function
2. Compute Friedman chi-squared statistic
3. Post-hoc Nemenyi test for pairwise comparison
4. Critical difference diagram

### 1.5 Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Matrix

Pairwise statistical significance testing:

```typescript
interface WilcoxonMatrixConfig {
  significanceLevel: number;  // α = 0.05
  correction: 'bonferroni' | 'holm' | 'none';
  cellDisplay: 'p_value' | 'symbol' | 'both';  // ✓✗ or p-values
}
```

---

## Tier 2: Interactive Exploration

### 2.1 3D Fitness Landscape

Interactive surface plots using JavaScript charting (Plotly.js or ECharts-GL):

```typescript
interface LandscapeConfig {
  function: string;            // e.g., 'shifted_ackley'
  resolution: number;          // Grid points per axis
  showContour: boolean;        // 2D contour projection
  showSearchPath: boolean;     // Overlay optimization trajectory
  colormap: 'viridis' | 'plasma' | 'material';
}
```

**Features:**
- Orbit controls (rotate, zoom, pan)
- Click-to-inspect fitness values
- Animated search trajectory overlay
- Toggle between surface/wireframe/contour

### 2.2 Search Trajectory Animation

Visualize optimizer population movement:

```typescript
interface TrajectoryConfig {
  playbackSpeed: number;       // Iterations per second
  showTrails: boolean;         // Ghost positions
  trailLength: number;         // Frames to retain
  colorByFitness: boolean;     // Heatmap coloring
  showBestPath: boolean;       // Highlight global best trajectory
}
```

### 2.3 Parallel Coordinates Plot

High-dimensional parameter space exploration:

```typescript
interface ParallelCoordConfig {
  dimensions: string[];        // Parameters to display
  colorBy: 'fitness' | 'algorithm' | 'iteration';
  brushing: boolean;           // Interactive range selection
  polylineOpacity: number;     // 0.0-1.0
}
```

### 2.4 Performance Profile

Dolan-Moré performance profiles:

```typescript
interface PerformanceProfileConfig {
  metric: 'time' | 'evaluations' | 'iterations';
  tau_max: number;             // Max performance ratio
  logScale: boolean;
}
```

### 2.5 Algorithm Radar Chart

Multi-criteria comparison:

```typescript
interface RadarConfig {
  criteria: Array<{
    name: string;              // e.g., 'Convergence Speed'
    min: number;
    max: number;
    optimal: 'min' | 'max';
  }>;
  normalize: boolean;
}
```

**Default Criteria:**
- Convergence Speed
- Final Precision
- Robustness (low std)
- Scalability (dimension performance)
- Computational Cost

---

## Tier 3: Dashboard Integration

### Unified Benchmark Dashboard

```html
<!-- Conceptual dashboard structure -->
<div class="benchmark-dashboard">
  <!-- Algorithm/Function Selector -->
  <select-panel algorithms="..." functions="..." />
  
  <!-- Multi-View Grid -->
  <grid-layout>
    <ecdf-chart />
    <convergence-chart />
    <violin-plot />
    <friedman-heatmap />
  </grid-layout>
  
  <!-- Statistical Summary Table -->
  <stats-table />
</div>
```

### Statistical Summary Table

| Algorithm | Avg | Std | Best | Worst | Median | FE | Time(s) | Rank |
|-----------|-----|-----|------|-------|--------|-----|---------|------|
| PSO | 1.23e-5 | 2.1e-6 | 8.9e-6 | 2.1e-5 | 1.1e-5 | 10000 | 0.42 | 1 |
| DE | 2.45e-5 | 3.2e-6 | 1.2e-5 | 4.3e-5 | 2.3e-5 | 10000 | 0.38 | 2 |
| SGO | 3.12e-5 | 4.5e-6 | 2.1e-5 | 5.8e-5 | 3.0e-5 | 10000 | 0.45 | 3 |

---

## Data Format Specification

### IOHprofiler-Compatible JSON Schema

```typescript
interface OptimizationRun {
  algorithm: string;
  function: string;
  dimension: number;
  run_id: number;
  seed: number;
  trajectory: Array<{
    iteration: number;
    evaluations: number;
    best_fitness: number;
    current_fitness?: number;
    best_position?: number[];
    timestamp_ms?: number;
  }>;
  final_result: {
    best_fitness: number;
    best_position: number[];
    total_evaluations: number;
    wall_time_seconds: number;
    converged: boolean;
  };
  metadata?: {
    hyperparameters: Record<string, any>;
    hardware: string;
    python_version: string;
  };
}

interface BenchmarkSuite {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  created_at: string;
  config: {
    runs_per_instance: number;  // Default: 30
    max_evaluations: number;
    target_precision: number;
  };
  results: OptimizationRun[];
}
```

### Export Format per Algorithm Category

```
docs/
├── api/
│   ├── swarm_intelligence.json    # mkdocstrings-generated
│   ├── evolutionary.json
│   ├── gradient_based.json
│   ├── classical.json
│   ├── physics_inspired.json
│   ├── social_inspired.json
│   ├── metaheuristic.json
│   ├── probabilistic.json
│   ├── constrained.json
│   └── multi_objective.json
├── benchmarks/
│   ├── sphere_30d.json            # Benchmark results
│   ├── rosenbrock_30d.json
│   ├── shifted_ackley_30d.json
│   └── summary_statistics.json
└── landscapes/
    ├── sphere_2d.json             # For 3D visualization
    ├── rosenbrock_2d.json
    └── ackley_2d.json
```

---

## mkdocstrings Integration for Python Docstrings

### Configuration (zensical.yml)

```yaml
# zensical.yml
plugins:
  - mkdocstrings:
      handlers:
        python:
          options:
            docstring_style: google
            show_source: true
            show_root_heading: true
            members_order: source
            separate_signature: true
            signature_crossrefs: true

markdown_extensions:
  - pymdownx.highlight:
      anchor_linenums: true
  - pymdownx.superfences
  - pymdownx.arithmatex:
      generic: true
  - admonition
  - attr_list
  - md_in_html
```

### API Documentation Page Structure

```markdown
# Particle Swarm Optimization

::: opt.swarm_intelligence.particle_swarm.ParticleSwarm
    options:
      show_root_heading: true
      heading_level: 2
      members:
        - __init__
        - search
        - _update_velocity
        - _update_position
```

---

## Project Structure

```
docs/
├── zensical.yml                  # Zensical config (mkdocs.yml compatible)
├── api/
│   ├── index.md                  # API overview
│   ├── swarm-intelligence.md
│   ├── evolutionary.md
│   ├── gradient-based.md
│   ├── classical.md
│   ├── physics-inspired.md
│   ├── social-inspired.md
│   ├── metaheuristic.md
│   ├── probabilistic.md
│   ├── constrained.md
│   └── multi-objective.md

items.title: Better toml use in the docs?
items.body:
### Description

Zensical's default TOML styling is imho sub-optimal for readability. 

For example, the a common [configuration for syntax highlighting](https://zensical.org/docs/authoring/code-blocks/#configuration) + arithmatex with zensical according to the docs is: 

```toml
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.highlight]
anchor_linenums = true
line_spans = "__span"
pygments_lang_class = true
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.inlinehilite]
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.snippets]
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.superfences]
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.arithmatex]
generic = true
```

But... surely instead the TOML below is more readable and thus preferred:

```toml
[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx]
highlight = { anchor_linenums = true, line_spans = "__span", pygments_lang_class = true }
snippets = {}
inlinehilite = {}
superfences = {}
arithmatex = { generic = true }
```

_Maybe_ this is stylistic, but I assume what's actually happening is that Zensical's documented TOML blocks are converted from a YAML source, and that conversion does not lead to the simplest output TOML. 

It's a minor issue in the grand scheme of things, but people will [copy + paste](https://github.com/search?q=%5Bproject.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.inlinehilite%5D+&type=code) these blocks verbatim into their zensical configs, so why not prefer the more readable versions?

_No response_

## Parent

#698

## What to build

Readers get the fixes that need only configuration, and the build becomes strict so later tickets cannot regress it:

- Snippets render without the 4–8 spaces of indentation they carry today (`pymdownx.snippets.dedent_subsections`), so a pasted block runs.
- Picking the Annotated tab once switches every Assignment/Annotated pair on the site (`content.tabs.link`), and tab anchors read as words (`tabbed.combine_header_slug` with a lower-case slugify).
- Hovering DDL, RLS, FK, PK, GUC, FFI and the other terms shows a definition (`abbr` + a glossary appended to every page through `snippets.auto_append` + `content.tooltips`). Glossary wording follows CONTEXT.md where it defines the term.
- `#NNN` references link to GitHub (`pymdownx.magiclink`, repo `syn54x/ferro-orm`); permalinks get a title (`toc.permalink_title`).
- Theme: `navigation.instant`, `.instant.progress`, `.tracking`, `.path`, `.footer`, `content.code.select`, `content.action.copy`; a third "follow system" palette toggle; `extra.social` (GitHub, PyPI); `extra.status` badges `new` and `deprecated`. `search.suggest` is removed.
- Plugins: `redirects` with anchor redirects replacing the hand-written stub for the old migrations page (the stub is deleted and each of its old anchors maps to the section that replaced it); `llmstxt`; `social` with background `#B7410E`.
- API reference: Pydantic's inventory; `filters = "public"`, `merge_init_into_class` + `ignore_init_summary`, `separate_signature`, `show_signature_annotations`, `signature_crossrefs`, `show_symbol_type_heading`/`_toc`, `summary`, `backlinks = "tree"`, `scoped_crossrefs`, `relative_crossrefs`, `show_source = false`; the `griffe-inherited-docstrings` extension (added to the docs and dev dependency groups); `show_overloads: false` and `parameter_headings` on the `Field` directive. `show_if_no_docstring` stays on until the API completeness ticket (#722) turns it off.
- The `**fields` parameters of `create`, `upsert`, `get_or_create` and `update_or_create` are annotated `**fields: Any`, so griffe stops warning.
- The docs build runs with `--strict` in the publish workflow and in a new docs job in CI.
- A new `tests/test_docs_site.py` builds the site strictly once per session and asserts that no snippet `<code>` block has every line sharing leading indentation.

Requires #699 (dependency upgrade) merged first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `zensical build --clean --strict` exits 0 with no warnings.
- [ ] The old migrations URL and each of its anchors redirect to the section that replaced them; the stub page is gone from the source tree and the sitemap.
- [ ] On a built page with two tab sets, the Assignment/Annotated tabs share a link group and their anchors are word slugs.
- [ ] A page using DDL shows an `<abbr>` with its definition.
- [ ] The rendered Model API page shows no source blocks, no dunder members, no `__ferro_*__` attributes, and linked type annotations in signatures.
- [ ] `Field` renders once, without its six overloads.
- [ ] `Relation.all()` and `.first()` show their inherited docstrings.
- [ ] The publish-docs workflow and the CI docs job build with `--strict`.

## Files owned

- Create: `docs/includes/abbreviations.md`, `tests/test_docs_site.py`
- Modify: `zensical.toml`, `.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `src/ferro/models.py` (the four `**fields` annotations only)
- Delete: `docs/pages/guide/migrations.md`

## Interfaces

- Consumes: nothing from other tickets
- Produces: Fixture `built_site` in `tests/test_docs_site.py`: session-scoped, returns the `Path` of a site built with `zensical build --strict` into a temporary directory. Used by the API completeness ticket (#722) and the enforce-guards ticket (#724).
- Produces: Helper `rendered_pages(built_site) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]` in the same module: yields `(url_path, html)` for every built page.
- Produces: Glossary file `docs/includes/abbreviations.md`, appended to every page; later tickets add terms to it only through the enforce-guards ticket (#724).
- Produces: `redirect_maps` table in `zensical.toml`; the nav ticket (#723) adds entries for the pages it moves.

## Test scenarios

- Happy path: `test_docs_site.py` builds the site strictly and passes.
- Error path: reverting `dedent_subsections` makes the indentation assertion fail on the quickstart page.
- Integration: requesting the old migrations URL with an anchor in the built site lands on the redirect page that points at the new section.

## Verify

```bash
uv run --no-sync zensical build --clean --strict
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_docs_site.py -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider
```

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately)

## Audit findings

<details><summary>Rows from the docs audit this ticket covers (file, line, rule, fix)</summary>

### Recommendation table

#### Griffe extensions

| Extension | What it does | Ferro evidence | Verdict | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataclasses` (built\-in) | Synthesizes `__init__` for stdlib dataclasses in static analysis | 71 `@dataclass` in `src/ferro` (PassReport, Report, ExecutedStatement, Check, RowPolicy…) | **Already on** (always loaded, nothing to add) | — |
| `unpack_typeddict` (built\-in) | Expands `**kw: Unpack[TD]` into named params | The only `Unpack` is `**extra: Unpack[pydantic.fields._EmptyKwargs]` in `ferro.Field` (an empty TypedDict) | **Skip**. It **crashes the build** (`KeyError: 'pydantic'`) unless you also set `preload_modules=["pydantic"]`, and that preload crashes griffe\-pydantic (see below). The payoff is removing one `**extra` param | `extensions = ["unpack_typeddict"]` \+ `preload_modules = ["pydantic"]` |
| `griffe_pydantic` | Labels models `pydantic-model`, adds Config / Fields / Validators sections, labels fields and validators | Public Pydantic models: `PoolConfig`, `DatabaseSettings`, `FerroSettings` (BaseSettings), `ferro.query.Row`, `Model` (`use_attribute_docstrings=True`) | **Consider** (adopt only with the caveats fixed) | `extensions = [{ griffe_pydantic = { schema = false } }]` \+ `preload_modules = ["pydantic_settings"]` |
| `griffe_warnings_deprecated` | Reads PEP 702 `@warnings.deprecated` and adds a deprecation admonition | Ferro's `_deprecations.deprecated` is a home\-grown decorator that is **never used**. Runtime deprecations (BackRef\[...] syntax, `state.py`) are `warnings.warn` calls the extension can't see. `requires-python >=3.13`, so stdlib `warnings.deprecated` is available | **Skip now; adopt together with** switching `_deprecations.deprecated` to wrap `warnings.deprecated` | `extensions = ["griffe_warnings_deprecated"]` |
| `griffe_inherited_docstrings` | Copies a parent member's docstring into an override that has none | `ferro.Relation` overrides `Query.all()` / `first()` without docstrings, so those headings render empty today | **Adopt** | `extensions = ["griffe_inherited_docstrings"]` |
| `griffe_public_redundant_aliases` | Treats `from x import y as y` as public | `ferro/__init__.py` declares `__all__`, the only `as`\-alias is `_deprecations as _deprecations` | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_public_wildcard_imports` | Treats `from x import *` names as public | No wildcard imports in `src/ferro` | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_runtime_objects` | Stores the live runtime object in `obj.extra` for custom templates | No custom templates | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_sphinx` | Uses `#:` comments above attributes as docstrings | `#:` is used only on `rowsecurity.py` module constants (`_COMMAND_CLAUSES`, `COMMANDS`, `_SETTING_KEY_RE`) and `checks.py` privates, none of them on an API page | **Skip** (reconsider if `rowsecurity.COMMANDS` gets documented) | `extensions = ["griffe_sphinx"]` |
| `griffe_typingdoc` | Reads param docs from `Annotated[..., Doc("…")]` (PEP 727\) | No `typing_extensions.Doc` anywhere. Loading it **crashed the build** (`KeyError: 'pydantic'`, the same Unpack path) and printed spurious `rowsecurity.py:100–103` param warnings | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_autodocstringstyle` | Sets the docstring parser to `auto` for objects from external packages | API pages render only `ferro.*` objects | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_generics` (3rd\-party) | Rewrites `T` to the bound type in subclasses | `ProjectedQuery(Query[T])` and `Relation(Query[T])` keep `T` unbound, so nothing to rewrite. Build: 0 changed lines | **Skip** | — |
| `griffe_modernized_annotations` (3rd\-party) | `Optional[X]` → `X \| None`, `List` → `list` | The handler's own `modernize_annotations` option does the same. Build: 0 changed lines (no `Optional`/`Union` reaches a rendered page) | **Skip** (use the option if ever needed) | — |
| `griffe_fieldz` (3rd\-party) | Injects dataclass/pydantic/attrs fields via `fieldz` | Overlaps griffe\-pydantic and the dataclasses extension. Build: 0 changed lines statically | **Skip** | — |

| `griffe_inherited_method_crossrefs` (3rd\-party) | Replaces an inherited method's docstring with "Inherited from \[Parent.m]" | Alternative to inherited\-docstrings for `Relation`. It links instead of duplicating | **Consider** as the alternative to inherited\-docstrings (not built) | `extensions = ["griffe_inherited_method_crossrefs"]` |
| `griffe_fastapi` (3rd\-party) | Documents APIRouter endpoints | No FastAPI | **Skip** | — |
| griffe\-tui | Terminal browser for Griffe data. Not an extension, and not on the Griffe extensions page | — | **N/A** | — |

#### mkdocstrings\-python options

Current: `docstring_style="google"`, `show_source=true`, `show_root_heading=true`, `show_root_full_path=false`, `show_category_heading=true`, `show_if_no_docstring=true`, `members_order="source"`; `inventories=[python]`.

| Option | What it does | Ferro reason | Verdict | Config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inventories += pydantic` | Cross\-links to Pydantic's Sphinx inventory | Fixes the one build issue (`pydantic.fields.FieldInfo` unresolved): the build reports **"No issues found"**. Links `BaseModel`, `Field`, `AliasPath`, `Discriminator`, `PydanticBaseSettingsSource` in signatures | **Adopt** | `inventories = ["https://docs.python.org/3/objects.inv", "https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/objects.inv"]` |

| `show_signature_annotations` | Shows types in signatures | A typed ORM whose docs push static typing (`QueryNode \| Predicate`, I\-8\). Today signatures show no types | **Adopt** | `show_signature_annotations = true` |
| `signature_crossrefs` | Links types inside separated signatures | Internal autorefs went from 67 to 439 and external from 245 to 1343 | **Adopt** | `signature_crossrefs = true` |
| `merge_init_into_class` (\+ `ignore_init_summary`) | Puts the `__init__` params in the class signature and drops the separate `__init__` entry | Removes 18 separate `__init__` entries (`Session`, `PassReport`, `Check`, `RowPolicy`, `FerroError`, `Query`…). | `show_symbol_type_heading` / `show_symbol_type_toc` | Adds class/meth/attr/func badges to headings and TOC | Pages mix classes, functions and attributes. Zensical CSS styles `doc-symbol` (61 rules) | **Adopt** | both `= true` |

| `summary` | Adds Attributes/Methods/Classes summary tables at the top of classes and modules | `Model` and `Query` have dozens of members. Adds 22 "Methods:" and 27 "Attributes:" summaries | **Adopt** | `summary = true` |
| `scoped_crossrefs` \+ `relative_crossrefs` | Enables `[Check][]` / `[.save][]` cross\-references inside docstrings | **284 Sphinx roles** (`:class:`, `:meth:`, `:func:`, `:attr:`) in Google docstrings currently render as **literal text** (e.g. Model's docstring shows ":class: \~ferro.checks.Check"). These options make the short Markdown replacement possible | **Adopt** (then convert the roles; runner.py 38, builder.py 29, cli/output.py 22, nodes.py 20, generate.py 20, registry.py 19, models.py 16, exceptions.py 13\) | `scoped_crossrefs = true`, `relative_crossrefs = true` |
| `filters = "public"` | Honours `__all__`, otherwise the underscore rule | Same anchors as today (verified id\-for\-id) but tracks `__all__` intent | **Adopt** (no visible change now; safer as modules grow) | `filters = "public"` |
| `show_overloads` (local) | Renders each `@overload` | `ferro.Field` has 6 overloads of \~50 params each, a wall of repeated text above the real signature | **Adopt locally on `::: ferro.Field`** | `options: show_overloads: false` |
| `parameter_headings` (local) | Gives each parameter an anchor, TOC entry and inventory entry | Enables links such as `ferro.Field(index)` / `Field(db_type)` from the guides. Global use would bloat every TOC | **Consider locally on `::: ferro.Field`** | `options: parameter_headings: true` |
| `show_inheritance_diagram` (local) | Mermaid class diagram per class | Useful only for the exception tree, which `exceptions.md` already draws as text. Globally it adds 26 diagrams | **Consider locally on `::: ferro.FerroError`**, otherwise Skip | `options: show_inheritance_diagram: true` |
| `show_source` | Embeds source with line numbers | Dominates page weight: model 608 kB → 174 kB, queries 997 kB → 289 kB with it off. Source is on GitHub | **Consider** `false` (a product decision) | `show_source = false` |
| `inherited_members` (local) | Renders inherited members | `Relation` would show 23 Query methods, duplicating the Query page. Backlinks plus inherited\-docstrings cover it | **Skip** (or local on `Relation` only) | — |
| `docstring_section_style` | table / list / spacy | `list` reads better at phone width for long Parameters tables (Field). Built fine | **Consider** `"list"` | `docstring_section_style = "list"` |
| `modernize_annotations` | Rewrites Optional/Union | No old\-style annotations reach rendered pages | **Skip** | — |
| `show_if_no_docstring` | Shows undocumented objects | Keep (current) | **Keep** | — |
| `members_order = "source"` | — | Keep (current) | **Keep** | — |

### Details

#### griffe\-pydantic (Consider)

What changed in the build (static mode):

- `PoolConfig`, `DatabaseSettings`, `Row` and `Model` get the `pydantic-model` label and a **Config** section (`frozen: True`, `extra: forbid`, and for Model `from_attributes`, `use_attribute_docstrings`, `arbitrary_types_allowed`). PoolConfig and DatabaseSettings also get **Fields** and **Validators** lists, and fields and validators get `pydantic-field` / `pydantic-validator` labels.
- `FerroSettings` (a `BaseSettings`) is **not** detected unless `preload_modules = ["pydantic_settings"]` is set. With the preload it is detected (5 models instead of 3 on the connection page).

Caveats that keep it at Consider:

1. **Field constraints vanish from the displayed value.** `max_connections = PydanticField(default=5, ge=1)` renders as `max_connections = 5`, and `name = Field(min_length=1)` renders as `name`. Today the constraint is visible. Unless each field's docstring states the constraint, docs lose information.
2. **A private validator leaks.** Model's Validators section lists `_validate_required_foreign_keys`.
3. `schema = true` silently turned the extension **off** in static mode: the output was identical to having no extension. A JSON schema would need dynamic import of `ferro`, which means building the Rust extension in the docs job.
4. `preload_modules = ["pydantic"]` crashes the build (`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`), so it can't be combined with `unpack_typeddict`'s workaround.

#### Sphinx roles are a bigger rendering bug than any extension

Google\-style docstrings across `src/ferro` contain 284 `:class:` / `:meth:` / `:func:` / `:attr:` roles. mkdocstrings doesn't interpret them, so Model's own docstring shows "as a tuple of :class: \~ferro.checks.Check objects". With `scoped_crossrefs` / `relative_crossrefs` on, they can become `[Check][ferro.checks.Check]` or `[Check][]`. The conversion is a separate docs task. No Griffe extension converts Sphinx roles (griffe\-sphinx handles only `#:` comments).

#### Deprecations

`ferro/_deprecations.py` defines `deprecated(reason=, since=, remove_in=, reference=)`, which wraps with `functools.wraps` and `warnings.warn`. Nothing uses it (`grep @deprecated` finds nothing), and griffe can't see it either way. Because Ferro requires Python ≥ 3\.13, `warnings.deprecated` is in the stdlib. If the helper is rewritten to return `warnings.deprecated(message)(obj)`, then type checkers flag call sites (PEP 702\) **and** `griffe_warnings_deprecated` renders the admonition. Adopt the extension in that same change. Until then it is a no\-op (built: 0 changed lines).

#### Remaining griffe warnings

`models.py:730/758/817/850` warn `No type or annotation for parameter '**fields'`. Fix this in the source by annotating `**fields: Any`. Don't silence it with `warn_missing_types = false`.

- Options set (`site-opts`): `doc-signature` blocks went from 20 to 315, internal autorefs from 67 to 439, external from 245 to 1343, backlink nodes from 0 to 577, and there are 300 heading badges and 740 TOC badges. items.title: 🎨 Palette: Add copy button to code blocks in documentation
items.body:
💡 **What:** Added `content.code.copy` to the `theme.features` list in `mkdocs.yml`.

🎯 **Why:** To improve the developer experience and usability of the documentation. Instead of manually selecting code in blocks to copy it, users will now see a handy "copy to clipboard" button on every code block.

📸 **Before/After:**
- Before: Code blocks in the MkDocs site were plain text and required manual text selection to copy.
- After: Code blocks now have a small icon in the top right corner that copies the entire snippet to the clipboard with one click.

♿ **Accessibility:** This also helps users who may have trouble using a mouse to precisely select text inside a code block.
